observations.statement: A finite benchmark can falsify a universal algorithmic claim but cannot establish a polynomial worst-case bound over all input lengths.
observations.support: This follows from the quantifier difference between finitely many tested inputs and a universal asymptotic statement.

observations.statement: A proposed polynomial representation is not a polynomial-time algorithm unless construction time, representation size, coefficient precision, evaluation time, and witness recovery are all polynomially bounded.
observations.support: Each omitted resource can encode exponential work or information.

observations.statement: Lower bounds for a direct encoding do not automatically refute a conjecture that permits polynomial-size auxiliary-variable lifts; the lower bound must quantify over the allowed lift class.
observations.support: The logical target of the lower bound must match the quantifiers of the registered hypothesis.

observations.statement: A hypothesis that merely asserts the existence of a polynomial-time SAT-deciding invariant without independently defining it is a restatement of P = NP, not progress toward it.
observations.support: The asserted invariant already is the missing polynomial-time decision procedure.

observations.statement: The Genesis survivors share one structural theme: they seek a polynomial-size exact lift into a mathematical class with an established polynomial-time decision algorithm.
observations.support: H001 uses bounded-treewidth dynamic programming, H002 submodular minimization, H003 linear programming over a totally unimodular system, and H004 constant-level semidefinite programming.

observations.statement: Any conjecture allowing an unrestricted polynomial-time transformer from SAT instances into a tractable target class is theorem-equivalent to P = NP when the target has fixed satisfiable and unsatisfiable instances and witness recovery may use the transformer's computation.
observations.support: Under P = NP, decide the input first and emit a constant yes-instance or no-instance of the target class. Conversely, the conjectured transformer plus the target algorithm decides SAT.

observations.statement: A literature frontier may be registered without a novelty claim when the exact statement, current restricted progress, and unresolved quantifier gap are all cited explicitly.
observations.support: H005-H008 and H011 are tied to primary-source records in references.json and labeled LITERATURE_FRONTIER.

observations.statement: A lower bound for a restricted proof system does not automatically transfer to a stronger system, and a lower bound for a direct encoding does not automatically survive extension variables.
observations.support: Simulation direction and the exact quantified model must be checked before transferring any lower bound.

observations.statement: Mutually incompatible hypotheses can both remain OPEN because OPEN records failure of the registered attacks, not probability, endorsement, or simultaneous consistency.
observations.support: H006 asserts a superpolynomial Extended Frege lower bound, while H011 asserts polynomial boundedness. At least one is false, but neither is refuted in the current record.

observations.statement: The next useful algorithmic hypotheses must restrict the allowed transformation or inference rules independently of a SAT oracle, so that solve-and-encode is syntactically impossible.
observations.support: H009 fixes bounded-radius local rewrite rules; H010 fixes an extension-enabled bounded-degree polynomial-calculus inference model and automatizer.
